description: Jerusalem started thinking the fame and the beauty were her own, and forgot who gave it to her. Most of us settle for the life we can produce on our own.
excerpt: Most of us settle for the version of our life we can produce on our own. We get competent and capable, and good at making things happen. Somewhere in there, we stop noticing that we've been running on our own power for a long time.
verse: "But you thought your fame and beauty were your own. So you gave yourself as a prostitute to every man who came along. Your beauty was theirs for the asking."
body_html:
The context around this verse is a long metaphor. God is speaking to Jerusalem. He describes finding her as an abandoned baby nobody wanted, raising her, washing her, clothing her, giving her beauty and wealth and status until she looked like royalty. Then verse 15 is where things shift. She started thinking the fame and the beauty were her own.

She forgot who gave it to her.

I've been thinking about this one recently. Lately I've felt the Lord asking me to spend more time with Him, and plenty of days I've chosen not to because I've been busy getting things done. And a lot of what I've been doing has been good.

That's the part that's convicting me. God has made it clear that yes, I can do some things on my own. I can even do some good things on my own. He's given me real talents and skills, and those don't disappear when I'm not sitting with Him. But underneath, He's been whispering something.

If I can do this much good on my own, what would my life look like if I pressed in and relied on His strength instead of mine?

I don't have the full answer, but it's a question I keep coming back to. Most of us settle for the version of our life we can produce on our own. We get competent and capable, and good at making things happen. Somewhere in there, we stop noticing that we've been running on our own power for a long time.

That's what happened to Jerusalem. Her drift didn't happen overnight. Over time she started assuming the gifts were hers to use however she wanted, and she forgot the One who gave them.

I'd rather catch that in myself now than look back later and realize I spent a whole life doing pretty good things in my own strength, when God was offering me so much more if I'd leaned on Him.

Where have you been relying on your own talent or capability when God is inviting you to press in and rely on His strength instead?
question: Where have you been relying on your own talent or capability when God is inviting you to press in and rely on His strength instead?
